definitions.gloss: freeloader; sponger; dependent lodger; person living off someone else
definitions.explanation: A person who stays at someone else's home without paying rent or contributing to expenses. Carries a mildly negative nuance of imposing on another's hospitality.

examples.japanese: ⟦{友人|ゆうじん}→友人：03649_yuujin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{居候|いそうろう}⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I'm freeloading at a friend's house.
As a freeloader, I can't really complain.

examples.japanese: ⟦{弟|おとうと}→弟：00572_otouto⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{仕事|しごと}→仕事：00480_shigoto⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{辞|や}めて⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{半年|はんとし}→半年：03139_hantoshi⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧{居候|いそうろう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{続|つづ}け→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧て⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦{困|こま}っている→困る：00861_komaru⟧。
examples.english: My younger brother has been freeloading for half a year since quitting his job, and it's become a problem.

notes:
Can function as both a noun and a suru-verb ({居候|いそうろう}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ = to freeload). The word has a self-deprecating quality when used about oneself, and a mildly critical tone when used about others. Historically, {居候|いそうろう} were common in the Edo period, when impoverished samurai or students would lodge with relatives or patrons.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {居候|いそうろう}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to freeload; to sponge off someone
- {居候|いそうろう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{身|み}→身：01764_mi⟧: the status of being a freeloader
- {居候|いそうろう}⟦{生活|せいかつ}→生活：01443_seikatsu⟧: life as a freeloader
- {居候|いそうろう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{続|つづ}ける→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧: to keep freeloading

SET EXPRESSION:
- {居候|いそうろう}{三杯目|さんばいめ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦そっと→そっと：03321_sotto⟧⟦{出|だ}し→出す：01087_dasu⟧: a freeloader should quietly present their bowl for a third serving — a humorous proverb about knowing one's place as a guest

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {厄介者|やっかいもの}: burden; nuisance — someone who causes trouble; more negative than {居候|いそうろう}
- ⟦{間借|まが}り→間借り：22383_magari⟧: renting a room — a paying arrangement, unlike freeloading
- ⟦{同居|どうきょ}→同居：09730_doukyo⟧: cohabitation; living together — neutral term without the freeloading nuance
